question: A scientific team from the Doñana Biological Station has analysed data from 38 years of bird censuses in Doñana and the Western Palaearctic, along with satellite images and meteorological data from 432 wetlands of international importance. This study shows that 9 of the 15 species analysed have experienced a decline in the last 40 years due to the loss of flooded areas in the marshes of the Doñana National Park.

The effects of Doñana’s deterioration extend beyond the boundaries of the protected area, meaning that wintering birds which spend periods nesting in the park are also affected. The Commission has been warning of the wetland’s deterioration since at least 2014, and in 2021 the Court of Justice of the European Union found Spain guilty of ignoring illegal systematic extractions in the area.
The serious deterioration of Doñana also jeopardises the achievement of the objectives set out in the Birds and Habitats Directives. In light of the above: 1.
What could the Commission do to ensure that water overexploitation in Doñana is stopped?
What steps could it take to ensure the recovery and restoration of Doñana’s ecosystem and biodiversity?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (8.5.2025) The Commission is aware of the issue raised by the Honourable Member and has taken legal action against Spain to address the problems of water overexploitation and biodiversity loss in Doñana through the correct application of the Habitats Directive1 and the Water Framework Directive2.

As a result, the Court of Justice of the EU found in a judgment of 24 June 20213 that Spain had failed to fulfil obligations under the above-mentioned Directives. It is for Spain to implement all the necessary measures to comply with the judgment of the Court under the supervision of the Commission.

The Commission sent to Spain a letter of formal notice4 under Article 260(2) of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union on 15 July 2022. Since then, the Commission has held several bilateral discussions with the Spanish authorities to discuss the measures they have taken and plan to take.

Spain has put in place a holistic plan to comply with the judgment, including measures in relation to illegal abstraction. The Commission will continue to closely monitor the implementation of the ruling and take any necessary step to ensure that it is fully complied with.

EU funding is available to help Spain solve this issue, for instance, both Recovery and Resilience Facility5 and the European Regional Development Fund6 can provide support for such type of investments.
